THE OPPORTUNITY

Make your catalogue work harder.

Manufacturing buyers often need more than a simple storefront. They compare specifications, check compatibility, request account terms, involve colleagues in approvals and reorder known products. Dealers and distributors may need their own prices, product access and documents.

Klirolabs designs and develops B2B ecommerce websites for manufacturers. We connect product discovery with the quote, ordering and operational workflows that make the experience useful for both buyers and your team.

Some businesses need a public product catalogue that generates qualified enquiries. Others need a logged-in dealer portal or a full ordering platform. Discovery establishes which model fits your sales process before development begins.

WHAT THE PLATFORM MAY NEED

Built around how business buyers actually buy.

The right feature set depends on your products, channel model and existing systems.

↗01

Technical product discovery

Structured specifications, variants, documents, filtering and comparison that help buyers identify the right product.

◈02

Business accounts and permissions

Dealer, distributor or customer access with appropriate catalogues, account terms and role-based actions.

⌘03

Quotes and repeat ordering

Request-for-quote journeys, saved lists, purchase order flows or quick reordering where they match the buying process.

✦04

Connected operations

Carefully planned links to ERP, product information, inventory, CRM and order systems where reliable integrations are available.

DISCOVERY BEFORE DEVELOPMENT

Start with the real buying journey.

We map who buys, who approves, how prices are determined and what happens after an order or quote request arrives. We also review the quality of product data, how inventory is managed and where manual work slows the team down.

That gives us a practical scope: public catalogue, protected account area, enquiry-led commerce or transactional B2B store. It also reveals what should be built first and what depends on data or process changes outside the website.

WHAT TO BRING TO THE FIRST CONVERSATION

Make the scope concrete.

A product catalogue sample, buyer types, current quote or order steps and a list of systems involved are enough to begin. We will identify where the website should simplify purchasing and where your team needs better tools behind it.

We can assess a new platform or improve an existing one without assuming a particular commerce technology before understanding the requirements.

COMMON QUESTIONS

Questions worth resolving early.

Can a B2B ecommerce website support dealers and distributors? +

Yes. We can plan separate account roles, catalogue access, pricing visibility and ordering permissions around your channel structure. The right setup depends on how you manage customers and territories today.

Do buyers have to pay online? +

No. A useful first release might let buyers build a basket and request a quote, place a purchase-order-backed order, or pay online. We choose the flow around your commercial terms and approval process.

Can the site connect with our ERP or product data? +

Potentially. We first review available APIs, data quality, ownership and update frequency. That assessment determines which catalogue, stock, pricing, customer and order data should sync and how.

What if our products have many variants or specifications? +

We structure product data, filters and comparison around the attributes buyers actually use. Complex configurations may need a guided selection or quote flow instead of a standard product page.

Can we start with a catalogue and add ordering later? +

Yes. A staged release can begin with discoverable products and qualified enquiries, then add accounts, quotes and transactions once the data and internal process are ready.
